name: Scripts
overview: Run your own scripts on server events.
description: Scripts runs your own commands when something happens on the server, such as playback, a new item, or a sign in. Each script can be narrowed with conditions and gets the event's details as environment variables.

versions.changelog:
## Added
- A chart at the top of the History tab shows how many runs succeeded and failed on each of the last 14 days, or 7 on a phone
- A Variables list under each step text field that takes placeholders. Select one to insert it at the cursor

## Changed
- Every section of the script editor starts closed and says what it holds under its heading, such as 2 steps, Everyone, or 4 conditions, all must match. General shows the script's description and whether it is Enabled or Disabled
- A section with a problem names it in its badge, such as Schedule ignored, 1 never matches, or No item kinds
- Item kinds is a panel under the trigger list. It shows only while a checked trigger has an item or the script runs for each library item, and it is cleared once none does. The Triggers heading shows All kinds or how many are chosen
- Test, Run now, and the trigger to test with are in a Testing section above Save
- The Variables section at the bottom of the editor is gone, since each step field lists the variables
- The trigger list and the History table show every row, and the page scrolls instead of the list
- Settings has two sections, Runs and History. Runs kept in the history is now Runs kept. The Docker and trust notes moved to the Run command docs
- A new script's scheduled task starts with no triggers. Add one under Scheduled Tasks. Scripts that already have a task keep its schedule
- Shorter help text on the Scripts and History tabs
- A script saved by this release with no schedule of its own cannot be read by an earlier release

## Developer
- GET Scripts/History/Days returns the runs that succeeded and failed on each of the last 14 days, without tests
- ScheduleMode has a None value, the default for a new script, which gives its task no starting triggers

## Changed
- The activity entry for failed runs has a generic name, Script runs failed, and an overview that says each fact once, such as Notify failed with the error The chosen collection no longer exists

## Developer
- skills/logging.md sets how activity entries and server log lines are written

## Fixed
- The run filter on the History tab read All Runs, and the clear button beside a secret's value was named Clear Value. They read All runs and Clear value, in sentence case like the rest of the page

## Developer
- Uses JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 12.4.3, after 12.4.1. Base fills a label into its own text in sentence case, such as a filter's All choice, a secret's clear button, and a column's resize handle

## Added
- The Scripts, History, and Settings tabs show their text in the viewer's language. Jellyfin's own words, such as day names, item kinds, and step names Jellyfin already has, come in every language Jellyfin has, and the rest is in US English until it is translated

## Changed
- Every label, badge, section title, and item kind is written in sentence case, as Jellyfin writes its own, such as Item kinds and Continues on error
- The trigger list, the path check under a command, and the errors Test and Run now report follow the page's language
- The activity entry for failed runs is written in the server's display language, such as 3 script runs failed

## Developer
- Uses JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 12.4.1, after 12.4.0. Base's translations build embeds the strings and Localization/casing.json, BaseHttp replaces JpkHttp, the failed run outcome uses ActivityOutcome's key constructor, and the controller reads the language with BaseTranslations.RequestLanguage in place of its language query parameters
- Catalog, Test, Run/{id}, and CheckPath take the language from ?language=, the X-Jellyfin-Plugin-Language header, or Accept-Language
- The project is split into Api, Configuration, Web, Assets, Models, Services, Localization, and Tasks folders, and every page file is embedded from Web
- The screenshot kit serves translations as { language, strings, casing }, with Base's own strings

## Developer
- Raises every GitHub Action in the workflows to its latest major version, pinned to a commit digest
- Builds the docs with Python 3.15 and mkdocs-material 9.8.2
- Renovate brings every update in one pull request, with Base on its own, and leaves the packages Jellyfin ships to the Jellyfin version

## Developer
- Uses JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 2026.11.21, which keeps a scrolling Data Table's frame in view and an open card's body on the plain surface, with no local code to replace
- Raises Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk to 18.12.0
- Pins every GitHub Action in the workflows to a commit digest

## Fixed
- A playback that ended without telling the server, such as an app that was force quit, was kept in memory with its item, session, and user until 5,000 had gathered. A playback that sends no report for 15 minutes is forgotten

## Developer
- PlaybackTracker drops a playback silent for AbandonedAfter on a sweep that runs at most once a minute, and its tests report the way a present client does

## Fixed
- In a run's details, long variable names such as JF_COMMUNITY_RATING ran over their values. The names share one column and wrap, and stack over their values on phones

## Developer
- Uses JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 2026.11.20, whose Definition List sizes the run variable names to a shared column and whose section titles show as written, so Item Kinds is written in Title Case. Nothing local is replaced
- The screenshot kit lives in tools/screenshots, with a catalog project that writes the plugin's own trigger catalog for the sample pages

## Changed
- In a condition row, Field, Operator, and the remove button line up with the bottom of the Value box
- The dashboard pages take Base's new buttons, sections, panels, and dialogs
- A run's steps show as a timeline with each step's result and output, and its variables as a list
- The webhook address has its own copy button beside it
- Each condition is a row of Field, Operator, and Value with a remove button. A number is a number box, a value with known choices is a list you search, and other values are tags inside the field
- The warnings for conditions sit under the rows
- The History table fills the window and scrolls inside, shows the trigger in its own column, and has Clear history beside the search
- Save sits in its own bar with no line above it, whose status says when there are unsaved changes
- Every Save is the same full width Save Bar, with any other actions in a full width row above it
- Secrets are rows of a name and a secret field. A stored value shows as dots, and removing the secret drops it
- Times such as the cooldown, a pause, a timeout, and a wait are set in hours, minutes, and seconds, and counts such as streams, retries, and runs at once with a slider
- Variables are a list with what each one holds, and selecting one copies it
- A step's condition and saved output are rows of labeled fields
- Check path shows its answer under the command
- A run's result, trigger, start, and length show as a list at the top of its dialog
- A stored secret has a Clear button that empties it on the next save
- The History columns keep the widths you drag them to
- A step condition's variable suggests the script's variable names as you type

## Fixed
- A Run now run showed as Manual in History. It shows as Run now
- Condition values offer their choices as you type
- Time, count, and webhook address fields keep their own layout on the server's dashboard

## Developer
- Uses JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 2026.11.19, with its Timeline, Definition List, Copy Field, Panel, Repeater, Data Table, Combo Box, Chip Select, and Tag Input in place of the local run steps, variables list, copy button, trigger option frames, condition rows, history table, variable name list, condition choices, and condition chips, and its Save Bar, Chip Select, and Repeater options in place of the local save failure line, Enter pick, secret name carrier, and name rewrite
- Base's Save Bar, Repeater, Record List, Slider Field, Duration Field, Field Row, Field Message, Record Selector, and Toast replace the local save bar, secret rows, variable cards, number inputs, step condition and output rows, path check line, and add step row, and scripts_shared.css keeps only two spacing rules
- The pages import Base only through scripts_common.js, which also holds the page wrapper
- The repository has contributor guides in starthere.md and skills/, and the design notes are the Architecture page of the docs

## Fixed
- The arrows on collapsible sections are back to their usual size

## Developer
- Uses JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 2026.11.13.3

## Changed
- Activity log entries are summed per outcome and share one shape. Failed script runs now leave one 3 Script Runs Failed entry naming each script and error with its count, instead of one entry per run

## Developer
- Uses JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 2026.11.13.2

## Changed
- The code and documentation are cleaned up, with no change to what the plugin does
- Built for Jellyfin 12.4. Servers on an earlier Jellyfin keep the previous release

## Developer
- Built against the Jellyfin 12.4.0 packages, which needed no code changes

## Added
- Webhook received trigger. Each script gets its own address, and a request must also carry a Jellyfin API key. Query parameters and JSON fields arrive as WEBHOOK_ variables
- Run now button, which runs the saved script at once whatever its triggers, filters, and cooldown say
- A step can save a command's output or an HTTP response, or one JSON field of it, for later steps to use as a placeholder
- Every step can have its own condition on any variable, and the new Stop here step ends a run early
- Run a script once for each library item or each user, picked by its item kinds, users, and conditions, with new fields such as Days since last played, Played by anyone, Has subtitles, and Days since last active
- A script can name another script to run when it fails
- New triggers for Playback passed a percentage, Switched to transcoding, Stream count reached, Transcode count reached, and New device seen
- Scripts have a description
- New templates for tagging unwatched movies, scanning from a webhook, and checking a service

## Changed
- A script on a schedule is now a Jellyfin scheduled task, listed under Scheduled Tasks in a Scripts section with the script's name and description. Set when it runs there. Existing schedules carry over as the task's starting triggers, except monthly ones, which Jellyfin has no trigger for and need one set
- Deleting a scheduled script hides its task at once and removes the files Jellyfin kept for it. The task itself goes when the server next restarts

## Developer
- Built with JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 2026.10.28.

## Fixed
- Run history is saved within a few seconds during a steady stream of runs, such as a library scan
- A cooldown is never claimed for a run that was not queued
- The docs explain how many distinct regex conditions stay fast

## Developer
- Built with JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base 2026.10.28.

## Fixed
- Renaming a secret keeps its value instead of quietly clearing it
- Secret values now live in their own encrypted file, so the plugin configuration any API client reads holds none, and a secret that shows up in a step message or command output is masked in the history and activity log
- A script on a scheduled task starting can no longer queue the same task forever, and tasks queued by scripts can no longer set each other off in a loop
- Favorite changed no longer fires when a user likes or dislikes an item
- Deleting a script saves only the deletion and leaves unsaved edits to other scripts for you to save or discard
- A schedule whose time is skipped by daylight saving runs when the clocks jump instead of failing and holding up other schedules, and a time just before midnight still runs if the check lands after it
- Clearing the history can no longer be undone by a save already in progress
- An interval schedule enabled again waits a full interval instead of running at once
- Test runs send messages meant for every session or every administrator only to your own sessions
- When an HTTP request runs out of retries, its last status and response body are kept
- Running another script skips a disabled script, and a nested failure is written to the activity log once
- An event value holding a path can no longer change which program a Run command step starts
- Append to file steps no longer fail when several runs write to the same file at once
- The editor checks number ranges before saving and says which field is out of range

## Developer
- Scripts are indexed by trigger once per saved configuration, schedule state is read from disk once, and new items waiting for metadata are released by their own update instead of being looked up every few seconds

## Features
- Run scripts on more than 45 server events, covering playback, library, collections, Live TV recordings, played and favorite changes, sessions, user accounts, scheduled tasks, plugins, settings, and the activity log
- Paused for a while and Playing for a while triggers, for jobs such as stopping playback left paused or asking whether someone is still watching
- Schedules that run a script every few minutes, daily at a time on chosen days, or monthly
- More than 20 built-in steps, including HTTP requests with presets for Discord, Slack, ntfy, Gotify, and Home Assistant, session messages, pausing and stopping playback, tags, collections, favorites, user sign out, library scans, and running programs on the server
- Filter by item kind, user, and conditions such as genre, year, play method, active transcodes, or time of day
- Encrypted secrets for tokens, templates for common scripts, export and import, test runs, and a searchable history

## Developer
- Initial release, built for Jellyfin 12.3 (target ABI 12.3.0.0).
